ownership.owns: Tiptap node definitions, command wrappers/chaining, defaults, TableKit, table insertion, HTML/Markdown integration, Tab row creation and whole-table deletion when all cells are selected. findings.fact: CellSelection is the canonical editor selection, not a second table selection store. It constructs one core range per selected cell's content, with the head cell first; generic anchor/head describe that primary range, while $anchorCell/$headCell retain the table endpoints. Transaction selection mapping calls the subclass. Mapping validates endpoints in the same table, preserves whole row/column extent when the table changes, and falls back to TextSelection when invalid.
findings.consequence: The reusable substrate capability is polymorphic selection participation in normal transactions, not table-specific fields in core.
findings.proof_limit: Read tests assert primary range and row/column insertion mapping; no exhaustive invalidation/collaboration proof.

findings.fact: CellSelection serializes as type cell plus cell endpoints, registers with Selection.jsonID, and overrides getBookmark. CellBookmark maps positions without a document and validates/resolves later, falling back to Selection.near. visible=false suppresses normal selection visibility via the contract; the table plugin supplies selectedCell node decorations.
findings.consequence: A feature-defined selection needs serialization/bookmark/fallback and paint integration to be a complete editor citizen. A pair of UI coordinates alone is insufficient.
findings.proof_limit: History implementation and browser selection rendering were not inspected or executed; bookmark support is an evidenced contract, not proven undo/native behavior.

findings.fact: TableMap.get caches by immutable table-node identity in a WeakMap (bounded fallback if unavailable). Offsets are table-relative. It owns span-aware rectangles, neighbor queries, unique-cell enumeration and malformed-grid/width problems. A changed table node recomputes its map; this is not an incremental topology-only cache.
findings.consequence: Keep one derived topology owner in the table feature, reusable by selection, commands, transfer and resize. Reusing the same table node can preserve its map when document positions outside the table change; content changes inside the table may invalidate it even when topology does not.
findings.proof_limit: No cache hit measurements or performance comparison; immutable identity reasoning only.

findings.fact: CellSelection.content creates a rectangular slice, clips spans at its boundaries, preserves surviving width attributes, and includes the table wrapper when every row/column is selected. Generic transaction replacement/deletion delegates to selection methods; CellSelection.replace maps each selected range after prior steps, inserts into the primary range and clears others. Table paste recognizes cell slices, tiles/clips to selected rectangles or grows from a single destination cell, then selects inserted cells. The keyboard delete command clears cell contents while retaining the table.
findings.consequence: Core supplies selection/transaction dispatch; the feature owns rectangular transfer and deletion semantics. These policies cannot be recovered from a flat generic from/to pair.
findings.proof_limit: No native copy/cut/paste performed. Browser clipboard caller/serialization, external spreadsheet formats and complete growth/isolation helper implementations were not audited.

findings.fact: tableEditing installs arrows, Shift-arrows, cell-content deletion and paste. Arrow navigation consults view.endOfTextblock; selection dragging is feature-owned and keeps a separately remapped transient drag anchor in plugin state. That transient anchor is not a second authoritative selection. Tiptap adds Tab/Shift-Tab, creates a row at the last Tab destination when possible, and intercepts deletion of an all-cell selection to delete the entire table.
findings.consequence: Structural navigation belongs with table topology; framework UX can choose different whole-table deletion and Tab behavior without inventing another selection model.
findings.proof_limit: Read arrow tests exercise command calls with EditorView, not real key dispatch or native caret parity. No Tiptap precedence runtime proof.

findings.fact: The optional resize plugin stores activeHandle and startX/startWidth in plugin state via transaction metadata. Mousedown and movement preview width through direct colgroup/table DOM writes; movement does not write colwidth document attributes. Mouseup or movement with no pressed button finishes, writes each distinct affected cell's colwidth in one document transaction when changed, then clears dragging metadata. Width is clamped to cellMinWidth; span and row-span traversal is table-specific.
findings.consequence: Transient interaction, render preview and persistent document edits have distinct lifetimes. This supports retaining table width policy in the feature and exposing any missing generic mounted interaction support separately.
findings.proof_limit: One document transaction is not an assertion about one undo item. History grouping, collaboration visibility and pointer/native behavior were not run.

findings.fact: Hover handling is disabled when the view is not editable. activeHandle remaps with association -1 and is invalidated when it no longer points at a cell. Window mouseup/mousemove listeners are removed by finish. The inspected plugin supplies no PluginSpec.view destroy callback, Escape/blur/pointercancel handler or dedicated cancellation operation. Remapping an invalid handle to -1 retains the dragging payload. A custom View does not replace the direct PM preview renderer.
findings.consequence: Do not promote this implementation as a complete generic gesture lifecycle. The general core PluginView destroy contract exists, but this resize plugin does not use it to own the temporary listeners. Preview customization and teardown/invalidation are concrete boundaries for the lead to compare locally.
findings.proof_limit: These are source-level lifetime/coupling observations, not reproduced crashes or proof of leaks. An actual deletion/unmount-during-drag scenario remains unverified.

findings.fact: Current Tiptap 3.30.3 imports and installs PM behavior, defines tableRole schema, exposes commands/kit/insertion and HTML/Markdown integration, and supplies a DOM TableView. It additionally retains cursor position after row/column deletion and registers its node view for non-resizable/read-only rendering so colgroups follow model changes. resizable defaults false; resize plugin inclusion is gated by configured resizing and editor.isEditable when plugins are constructed.
findings.consequence: Treat Tiptap as an integration/UX layer over the same table engine, with real extra rendering and cursor policy. It is not an independent selection, topology or resize state machine; do not reduce all its current structural commands to unchanged one-line wrappers.
findings.proof_limit: Current lockfile resolves tables 1.8.5/state 1.4.4, matching inspected package versions. No installation/runtime, browser proof or released-artifact identity check. Markdown tokenizer changes were read in the diff but not audited end-to-end.

findings.topic: Resize handle cardinality and hit-testing ownership
findings.fact: columnResizing has one activeHandle in its keyed editor plugin state. Its decorations callback emits handles only while activeHandle > -1. handleDecorations walks that active table's rows at the selected column, adding a widget at each qualifying cell's end: only where the column is a cell boundary and only once per row-spanning cell. It adds a dragging node decoration to the same qualifying cells while dragging. Thus this is transient per-cell paint along one active boundary, not a single table overlay and not permanent bottom/right controls in every cell.
findings.cardinality: With H unmerged rows and an active column boundary, source constructs H handle widgets (and H cell decorations while dragging). Generally widget count is <= H because spans suppress duplicates/non-boundaries. No active boundary means the callback returns no handles. Counts are derived from source, not DOM/performance measurements.
findings.hit_testing: Editor-view mousemove walks event.target ancestors to TD/TH, tests getBoundingClientRect left/right distances against handleWidth, then edgeCell uses view.posAtCoords with an offset away from collapsed borders. Right edge maps to that cell; left edge maps to the preceding grid cell, and the table's first-column left edge returns -1. lastColumnResizable can suppress the last boundary. The supplied PM stylesheet sets handle pointer-events:none and positions it on the cell's physical right edge; handles are paint, not hit targets under that stylesheet.
findings.ownership: Feature plugin owns hit-testing, active boundary, gesture and shared preview; cell DOM carries transient decorations. Default PM/Tiptap TableView builds table/colgroup/tbody, without per-cell resize controls or a separate overlay. This is column resizing only: no bottom-edge row-height resize owner is present in these inspected implementations.
findings.local_comparison_limit: Lead-supplied local baseline: copied TableCellResizeControls mounts bottom+right in every cell plus first-column left, with shared table preview. This shard did not inspect that local implementation; lead owns its verification and final cut. PM demonstrates centralized hit-testing and transient boundary paint, but does not demonstrate an equivalent row resize feature.
findings.proof_limit: No browser interaction, actual mounted-node count, touch/pointer device, accessibility or speed proof. PM CSS behavior is stated for the supplied stylesheet; no assumption it is imported by every Tiptap app.

findings.fact: At remote HEAD eb974ea2f6e6eae10d987bcba4d32f80ca4f1ca8, deleteColumn/deleteRow wrap PM dispatch with keepCursorInTable, which maps the original table position, checks whether the selection still belongs to that table, and otherwise places TextSelection near its end. Table.addNodeView registers the configured View when resizing is inactive, passes merged HTMLAttributes, and leaves resizable registration to PM. Current tests assert last-row/column cursor retention (including another table below), non-resizable/read-only programmatic colgroup updates, and multi-cell canonical deleteSelection.
findings.consequence: Current framework ownership includes document-command UX and model-to-view synchronization beyond options/aliases. Separating sizing rendering lifetime from the optional resize gesture is a source-backed comparison candidate.
findings.proof_limit: Read tests were not executed. Tests state intended assertions; they do not prove actual current browser behavior or full keyboard handler precedence.

strongest_justified_promotion_cut.status: Evidence-backed candidate for lead comparison; not a local verdict or selected implementation.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.promotion: If Plite's canonical selection cannot host feature-defined range, mapping, replacement, bookmark/restore and paint semantics, change that core contract and let table selection participate in it.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.cut: Cut any parallel authoritative table-selection store and table-specific remapping/transfer interception that exists only to compensate for that core gap. Keep CellSelection semantics and TableMap/topology in the optional table owner.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.current_upstream_flow: CellSelection.create(doc, anchorCell, headCell) -> tr.setSelection(...) -> ordinary Transaction.selection remapping -> CellSelection.map/replace/content/bookmark.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.material_benefit: One authoritative selection and transaction integration can remove caller coordination across typing, deletion, transfer and state restoration.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.strongest_counterargument: A full subclass protocol adds registration, validity/fallback, replacement, bookmark and rendering obligations. PM alone does not prove a new Plite protocol is needed, nor that its exact class API is the right design. If existing Plite selection/reference/transfer capabilities already provide these laws with one owner, adding another protocol would be needless machinery.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.resize_related_cut: Unify committed and preview rendering ownership when they diverge; avoid a second hard-coded renderer that bypasses a configurable node view. Upstream source supports this local comparison, not a generic core table-resize API.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.unresolved_by_this_shard: The lead must establish the actual local duplication/gap and decide the smallest durable core contract and adoption cost.
strongest_justified_promotion_cut.handle_related_cut: Compare deleting permanent per-cell resize hit controls in favor of one feature-owned hit-testing/gesture owner and transient boundary paint. PM is evidence for that ownership split, not evidence for a single overlay or for removing row-height/keyboard jobs.

rejected_ideas.reason: The inspected architecture integrates custom selection through a generic contract while span geometry, transfer and widths stay in an optional feature. No independent non-table consumer is evidenced.

rejected_ideas.reason: A table rectangle requires multiple cell ranges, clipped span-aware content and feature fallback policy. Flat from/to loses this behavior.

resize_input_policies.scope: PM columnResizing at eb522f25959a1e4515a4ff5ce7e3a939f19c55e9 and current Tiptap delegation.

keyboard.observation: Resize plugin props only register mousemove, mouseleave and mousedown; window handlers use mousemove/mouseup. No keyboard resize or Escape handler is present. Table arrow/Tab/delete navigation is separate and is not evidence of keyboard-accessible resizing.

rtl.observation: Inspected resizing code uses physical left/right cell edges, previous map column for left-edge hits, and width=startWidth+(clientX-startX). Supplied CSS uses right:-2px. No direction/RTL branch appears in this resize owner. Open issue #333 reports wrong-cell/wrong-column behavior in RTL; that runtime report was not reproduced.

cancel.observation: Mouseup and mousemove with no pressed button finish and commit; they are not cancellation. Mouseleave clears inactive hover only. No Escape, pointercancel, blur rollback or plugin destroy cleanup is provided in this owner. No unmount or deletion failure is claimed without runtime proof.

read_only.observation: PM hover, mouseleave and mousedown check view.editable. Already-installed window move/finish closures do not re-check editable. Tiptap includes resizing only when configured resizable and editor.isEditable during plugin construction; its non-resizable node view still supports rendering. Current colgroup test changes editor to read-only then executes a column command and asserts synchronized colgroup. No claim is made that toggling editability during a drag cancels it.
